description: The closed vocabulary of personas a PRD user story may name. prd-writer validates every 'As the {persona} ...' story against this list -- see docs/product/orchestrator/PRODUCT.md, 'Personas'.

personas.name: Stakeholder
personas.role: Product manager, designer, founder, or business stakeholder who opens the issue that starts a piece of work, and approves the PRD that comes back.

personas.name: Engineer
personas.role: Software engineer responsible for the design, the code, and the quality of the change; approves the build plan before any of it is written.

personas.name: Reviewer
personas.role: Tech lead, staff engineer, or peer who approves at gates a Stakeholder or Engineer does not: sizing, design, test spec, PR.

personas.name: Standards Owner
personas.role: Architect, platform team, or technical lead who owns the standards the pipeline enforces, and approves proposed changes to them.

personas.name: Security Owner
personas.role: Security engineer, AppSec lead, or compliance officer who approves any change flagged as touching a security-sensitive surface.

personas.name: Data Owner
personas.role: Owner of a data domain's content, schema, and lifecycle; approves any change that includes a data migration.

personas.name: System actor
personas.role: The role a capability is written against when its primary actor is genuinely automation (a scheduled job, an audit logger), not a person -- so automated capabilities go through the same product-led pipeline as everything else.
qualifying_test: Names a real human stakeholder who benefits, even indirectly -- the 'so that' clause states that benefit. If no human can be named, it is technical preference, not product.

Is expressible as Gherkin acceptance criteria with an observable Then-clause (a row appears in a table, an alert fires, a number increases on a dashboard). If the only observable outcome is that code is structured a certain way, it is technical design, not product.
Names a stable automated role, not an implementation choice or a tool user -- 'As the audit log writer' qualifies; 'As the database' or 'As a developer' does not.
